Brief Facts as per the plaint:-

2. Plaintiff claims to be the owner of property bearing no. Khasra no. 363, Plot/House no. D-488,
situated at Pul Prahladpur, New Delhi- 110044 measuring 50 sq. yards, (hereinafter referred to as "the suit property") residing on the ground floor with her two unmarried sons.
Her elder son (Defendant No. 1) and his wife (Defendant No. 2) reside on the second floor as licensees.

It is stated that plaintiff purchased the suit property from her husband on 18.07.1995 via General Power of Attorney, Agreement to Sell, Affidavit, and Receipt.
The property was constructed with her own earnings and stridhan.
Plaintiff and her late husband ran a tea stall "Chauhan Tea Stall" for over 28 years at Shop No. A-8, Opposite D-178, Okhla Phase-I , New Delhi ( hereinafter referred to as "the shop").
The shop was given to the plaintiff and is her only source of livelihood.
A separate property at Hari Nagar, Badarpur, was purchased in the name of defendant no.1 but with the joint earnings of the plaintiff and her husband.
Defendant no.1 allegedly sold this property without informing the plaintiff.
It is claimed that after plaintiff's husband died in 2012.
Defendant no.1 began operating the tea stall but stopped supporting the plaintiff financially.
Despite repeated requests, he neither vacated the shop nor paid the agreed monthly maintenance of Rs. 5000/- and house rent of Rs.10,000/-, along with arrears of Rs.3,00,000/-.
It is claimed that defendant has threatened the plaintiff and her sons, leading to police complaints and publication of a public disownment notice on 11.11.2016.
Plaintiff had also filed complaint against defendants before the police vide DD no. 32B dated 31.10.2017.
Thereafter, plaintiff sent a legal notice dated 31.12.2017 to the defendant to vacate the suit property.
However, defendants failed to vacate the suit property.
Hence, the present suit.

Per contra, defendants claim that Ex.PW-1/2 (colly) (OSR) i.e. copy of general power of attorney,
agreement to sell, affidavit and receipts, dated 13.07.1995, do not confer any right, title or interest to the plaintiff in the suit property.
It is claimed that the suit property was purchased by Lalit Singh Chauhan i.e. father of defendant no.1 and father in law of defendant no.2.
Defendants have been residing in the suit property for more than 18 years.

Since, defendant no.1 is the legal heirs of late Sh. Lalit Singh Chauhan, along with plaintiff and brothers of defendant no.1, therefore, he is equally entitled to a share in the suit property, along with the plaintiff.

21. Perusal of the record reveals that plaintiff has claimed absolute ownership over the suit property by relied upon Ex.PW-1/2 (colly) (OSR) i.e. copy of general power of attorney, agreement to sell,
affidavit and receipts, dated 13.07.1995.

These documents, however, do not confer any right, title or interest in favor of the plaintiff, with respect to the suit property, since they Digitally signed by yashu yashu khurana Date:
khurana 2025.08.13 16:21:03 +0530 CS SCJ 848/18 NIRMALA DEVI Vs. PRADEEP CHAUHAN Page no. 13 of 16 are unregistered documents.
It is an admitted fact that the suit property was originally purchased by plaintiff's husband i.e. late Sh. Lalit Singh Chauhan.

Defendant no.1, his brothers and plaintiff are the legal heirs of Sh.
Lalit Singh Chauhan.

Since Sh. Lalit Singh Chauhan, has died interstate, therefore,
the suit property shall devolve upon the legal heirs of Sh. Lalit Singh Chauhan, as per the rules of interstate succession, under Hindu Succession Act.

Till the time the suit property is partitioned and shares of the legal heirs of Sh. Lalit Singh Chauhan are determined, neither plaintiff nor defendants can claim absolute ownership, with respect to any portion of the suit property.
Plaintiff has also miserably failed to prove that one room on the second floor of the suit property was given to defendants under a licensee.
Plaintiff has also failed to prove that suit property was constructed by her earnings and stridhan.
Therefore, plaintiff has failed to discharge the onus of proving the issue at hand.
Accordingly, issue no.2 is decided against the plaintiff and in favour of the defendants.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The shop was given to the plaintiff and is her only source of livelihood.
Defendant no.1 allegedly sold this property without informing the plaintiff.
It is claimed that after plaintiff's husband died in 2012.
Defendant no.1 began operating the tea stall but stopped supporting the plaintiff financially.
Despite repeated requests, he neither vacated the shop nor paid the agreed monthly maintenance of Rs. 5000/- and house rent of Rs.10,000/-, along with arrears of Rs.3,00,000/-.
Plaintiff had also filed complaint against defendants before the police vide DD no. 32B dated 31.10.2017.
Thereafter, plaintiff sent a legal notice dated 31.12.2017 to the defendant to vacate the suit property.
To discharge the onus of prove,
plaintiff contended that the shop bearing no. D-178, Okha Phase-I, New Delhi- 110020 , was purchased by her late husband namely Lalit Singh Chauhan and after his death, defendant no.1 has been in possession of the said shop.

7 17.
It is a settled principle of law that possession is nine points of law and anyone who claims against the person in possession must prove a better title.
The onus of proving issue no.1 and 3 was cast upon the Digitally signed by yashu yashu khurana
However, she has miserably failed in discharging the onus of proving the issues at hand.
Since Sh. Lalit Singh Chauhan, has died interstate, therefore,
the suit property shall devolve upon the legal heirs of Sh. Lalit Singh Chauhan, as per the rules of interstate succession, under Hindu Succession Act.
Till the time the suit property is partitioned and shares of the legal heirs of Sh. Lalit Singh Chauhan are determined, neither plaintiff nor defendants can claim absolute ownership, with respect to any portion of the suit property.
Plaintiff has also miserably failed to prove that one room on the second floor of the suit property was given to defendants under a licensee.
Therefore, plaintiff has failed to discharge the onus of proving the issue at hand.
